Cancel.description:
Stops a running run's main code, without running flow code: in its turn's one commit it cancels the armed
`Continue`, marks the run cancelling and arms a cleanup `Continue` with the flow's retry policy and its own
correlation id, keeping the input, the journal and the replies; a cancelling, done or cancelled run ignores it,
writing nothing. It waits for the turn before it in the mailbox and does not undo effects already made; the
cleanup, [`Flow::on_cancel`], runs in later turns and marks the run cancelled when it succeeds. Sending it only
queues it: read the run's status to learn that it was cancelled.
Cancel.title: Cancel

Continue.description:
Starts or recovers a running or cancelling run; a done or cancelled run ignores it. Sent by a host, it cancels
the armed continuation and arms a fresh one with the flow's retry policy, without running flow code; the armed
one replays the flow, or its cleanup once the run is cancelling, and executes its next step.
Continue.title: Continue

Reply.description:
The reply of a target to a request of the run, sent with [`ReplyTo::send`]. The run keeps the first one from the
request's target and ignores any other, without running flow code; a cancelling run closes only a cleanup wait
with it.

request.description: The id of the request's message, saved with its send entry.

value.description: The reply's JSON, `null` included; required, so a missing value is not `null`.

Reply.title: Reply

CreateKind.description: How a send entry created its target before its message: as an independent actor or as a child of the run.

oneOf.description: Created with no parent, as [`Turn::create_raw`] does: an actor that exists already is left untouched.
Created as a child of the run, as [`Turn::create_child_raw`] does: an actor owned elsewhere rejects the commit.

FlowReply.description: A reply a run kept for a request of one of its send entries.

request.description: The id of the request's message.

value.description: The reply's JSON, `null` included; required, so a missing value is not `null`.

FlowStatus.description: The phase of a run (ADR 0044): its main code runs while it is running, its cleanup while it is cancelling.

oneOf.description: Steps remain, or the flow has not yet returned.
A run that took `Cancel` while running and whose cleanup, [`Flow::on_cancel`], has not yet succeeded.
The flow returned `Ok` after replaying every saved entry; the run keeps its state until it is deleted.

A run ended by `Cancel` whose cleanup succeeded; it keeps its state until it is deleted, and ignores
`Continue`, `Reply` and `Cancel`.

JournalEntry.description: One saved entry of a journal.

oneOf.description: The saved result of a step.

id.description: The step id: 1 through 100 characters of `A-Za-z0-9._~-:`, unique in its journal.

result.description: The JSON result of its closure, `null` included.

oneOf.description: A durable sleep of [`Step::sleep`] until a store time: the flow goes on in the first turn at or after it.

id.description: The sleep id, from the same namespace as the step ids.

until.description: When the sleep ends; at most `MAX_INSTANT`.

oneOf.description:
A message of [`Step::send`], enqueued in the commit that saved this entry, after the create of its target if
any. Neither the message nor the initial state is saved.

create.description: How the target was created in the same commit; absent or null: not created.

id.description: The send id, from the same namespace as the step ids.

message.description: The id of the message; unique among the sends of both journals.

reply.description: Whether the message is a request of [`Step::request`] that a reply answers; absent: false.

oneOf.description:
A wait for the replies of earlier requests: one request, or a join of several or of mode first, without or
with a deadline. Its saved selection, not the replies kept later, is what replay returns.

id.description: The wait id, from the same namespace as the step ids.

mode.description: Every reply or the first one.

outcome.description: How it ended; absent or null: it is open.

received.description: The requests whose replies it selected, in the order of `requests`; absent: none. At most 100.

requests.description: The message ids of the requests it waits for: 1 through 100, unique.

until.description: Its deadline; absent or null: none. At most `MAX_INSTANT`.

SignUp.description: The input of the test flow.

WaitMode.description: Whether a wait needs every listed reply or the first one.

oneOf.description: The first accepted reply of any request.

state.description:
The state of a run: its input, the journal of saved results, its status, the id of its armed `Continue`, the
replies it kept and the journal of its cleanup.

On the wire: `{"input":{"user":"u1"},"journal":[{"kind":"step","id":"account","result":"a1"}],
"status":"running","armed":"m1","replies":[],"cleanup":[]}`; `journal`, `status`, `armed`, `replies` and `cleanup`
default to empty, running, null, empty and empty, so a state of an earlier release decodes. A decoded state is
checked (ADR 0044): each journal holds at most 1000 entries with unique valid ids, sleeps and deadlines end at most
at `MAX_INSTANT`, send message ids are unique across both journals, waits and replies name earlier requests
consistently, at most 2000 replies, and the status agrees with `armed`, `cleanup` and any open wait. The schema
describes field types, presence, lengths, patterns and names; the checks across fields are typed checks, not part of
it. A journal given at the create is trusted as progress: replay checks its order and result types against the
flow's code, not whether its effects happened.

armed.description: The id of the armed `Continue`; absent or null when none is armed, and always on a done or cancelled run.

cleanup.description: The cleanup's entries, with ids of their own; at most 1000; absent: none.

journal.description: The saved entries, in the order the flow reached them; at most 1000, with unique ids; absent: none.

replies.description: The replies kept for requests, one per request; at most 2000; absent: none.

status.description: Running, cancelling, done or cancelled; absent: running.

state.title: FlowState
